title: Solve missing-number fraction division
intro: An unknown dividend, divisor and quotient have different roles. Use divisor × quotient = dividend to connect them.
html:
Solve missing-number fraction division

An unknown dividend, divisor and quotient have different roles. Use divisor × quotient = dividend to connect them.

The given quotient can itself be a fraction. Use exact fractions for every step rather than rounding a decimal approximation.

A method to try

  1. Identify whether the blank is the dividend, divisor or quotient.
  2. Use dividend = divisor × quotient, or divide the dividend by the known factor.
  3. Substitute the exact fraction back into the original division.

Worked examples

2/7 ÷ □ = 22/49

The divisor is (2/7) ÷ (22/49) = (2/7) × (49/22) = 7/11.

□ = 7/11

Check: 2/7 ÷ 7/11 = 22/49.

□ ÷ 6 = 7/54

Multiply the quotient by the divisor.

□ = 7/9

Check: 7/9 ÷ 6 = 7/54.

A mistake to watch for

Do not apply the reciprocal rule to whichever fraction is nearest the blank. Write the multiplication relationship first.

Check and explain

Equivalent simplified or unsimplified fractions can represent the same answer.
examples: Multiply the quotient by the divisor.
